subject: TheraHealth pilot - hosting posture decision & committed GPU ask
messages:
From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@therahealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on Private vs Dedicated for pilot (TheraHealth)

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and our engineering lead reviewed the architecture notes and we need a recommended approach for the 12-week pilot: whether we should go Private (VPC, customer-managed control plane) or Reserved/Dedicated capacity on Redwood. Key constraints:

- PHI-sensitive workloads, must be isolated with SOC2-compatible evidence
- Peak inference: ~120 concurrent sessions (short prompts, avg 60 tokens)
- Expected throughput: ~1.2M tokens/day with spikes during business hours
- Strict uptime requirement for demo (SLA discussion)

Can you provide a concrete sizing recommendation (GPUs, burst vs reservation, expected latency per request) and a procurement timeline? Procurement will need line-item costs to compare to our internal on-prem estimate. I attached our pilot requirements.

Thanks,
Rajiv Singh
VP Product Operations
TheraHealth
attachments: thera_health_requirements.pdf
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@therahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on Private vs Dedicated for pilot (TheraHealth)

Rajiv —

Appreciate the clear requirements and the PDF. High level recommendation for a 12-week pilot: start on Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) with an option to move to Private if you need a customer-managed control plane for regulatory reasons or long-term data residency. Summary: 

- Dedicated as default for pilot: faster onboarding, predictable latency/SLOs, no change to your infra. We can guarantee a dedicated pool sized to meet your peak concurrency.
- Private for longer-term or if your security team insists on a VPC/on-prem control plane — recommended after pilot once we collect audit logs and finalize KMS integration.

Actionable sizing proposal (ballpark for procurement line items):
- Committed: 6 x A100 80GB-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated cluster (handles baseline 120 concurrent sessions with headroom)
- Burst window: allow +2 GPUs on burst policy for extreme spikes (hourly auto-burst)
- Expected median p99 latency: ~120–180ms for 60-token prompts (model variant dependant)
- Prefix caching and batching assumed enabled to reduce per-token CPU/GPU overhead

I asked Karthik to run a short capacity sheet with both Dedicated and Private templates and a cost delta. Attaching a proposed sizing sheet and SLA exception form for procurement to review.

Next steps:
- I can circulate finalized line-item pricing and timeline today if procurement wants pricing for a PO.
- If security requires Private immediately, we’ll provide an on-prem checklist and estimated lead time (~6–8 weeks).

Marissa (cc) — please add committed pricing and a quick procurement timeline (PO -> deploy) to the sheet.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Manager, Solutions
Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed_sizing_sheet.xlsx, sla-exception-form.pdf

Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on Private vs Dedicated for pilot (TheraHealth)

Folks —

I ran a quick worksheet (attached) with assumptions derived from Rajiv's requirements. Short summary and numbers to drop into procurement: 

- Workload assumptions used: 120 concurrent sessions, avg 60 tokens, 1.2M tokens/day, 12-week duration
- Dedicated cluster sizing: 6 x A100-80GB equiv (baseline) + 2 x A100 for burst (autoscale policy). Estimated committed monthly spend: $115k/month (GPU infra + orchestration + egress estimates).
- Private deployment estimate (customer-managed control plane + dedicated infra): 8 x A100-80GB equiv upfront with operational uplift. Estimated equivalent monthly run-rate after setup: $150k/month (includes support & HSM/KMS integration amortized).
- Procurement line-items: GPU capacity, reserved-commit term (3 months), premium SLA, SOC2 evidence bundle, optional on-prem migration fee.

Risks & notes: 
- If TheraHealth needs strict key custody (HSM), Private will add 2–3 weeks to lead time for certs and validation.
- We recommend a Dedicated pilot with an explicit 30-day review to switch to Private if security gating fails.

I attached the detailed proposed_sizing_sheet.xlsx with per-GPU math and a short cost comparison table.

- Karthik
Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Rajiv —

Short update for procurement: Attached is a distilled line-item summary: 3-month committed Dedicated cluster (6 A100 equiv) + 30-day burst buffer (2 GPUs) + premium SLA add-on. Estimated POable amount for the pilot: $345k (covers 3-month term). If you decide to elect Private up-front we’ll add a one-time migration/setup line item (~$48k) and move to 8 GPUs to accommodate control plane overhead.

Procurement timeline (if Dedicated pilot):
- Day 0: PO received
- Day 2–4: Contract signature and billing setup
- Day 5–9: Dedicated cluster provisioning and smoke tests
- Day 10: Pilot kick-off

If you want, I can loop in our compliance lead to run the SOC2 evidence checklist with your security team this week. Let me know which hosting posture you want on the PO and we’ll generate a formal quote + DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Manager, Solutions
Redwood Inference
